rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: Which kinds of old photos do people struggle to retrieve (what photo types or characteristics are associated with retrieval difficulty)?
rows.gap: the two AI coders agreed too little on outcome to report it as a finding; the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
People most often struggle with sentimental photos when search did not understand what they typed, not a specific visual “type” of photo [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]].

27% (13 of 48) of sentimental stories first went wrong at Stage 5 (search did not understand it) [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]].

One parent tried “vomit” for “photos of $son where they were vomiting (cutely)” and got “no result for vomit” [[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]].

Because the two AI coders agreed too little on outcome and on what details people remembered (question 2.1), this cannot say which photo “types” are hardest, only where retrieval breaks [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

Interpretation: Utility photos show counts only; Stage 0 (not there to find) appears in 8 of 21, and Stage 2 (what they remember) in 4 of 21 [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:utility]] [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]].

Interpretation: Unclear-class stories also cluster at Stage 5 and Stage 6, each at 33% (15 of 46) and 13% (6 of 46) respectively [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]] [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:unclear]].

Interpretation: Shares are of public stories, not user success rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

rows.gap: the stories hold nothing on where in the journey this happens; too few stories to quote — only 0 matched; the two AI coders agreed too little on outcome to report it as a finding; the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
People most often remember what is in the photo — the subject or type — followed by when and who, with where trailing. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]]

41% (47 of 115) mention what; 21% (24 of 115) mention when; 12% (14 of 115) mention who; 10% (11 of 115) mention where; event and capture each appear in 5% (6 of 115) and 3% (4 of 115), and perceptual and meaning each in 3% (4 of 115) and 2% (2 of 115). [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]]

One person said they “knew I'd seen one recently(ish) but couldn't think how I'd figure out where,” then searched by object (“medlar”) and found it. [[story|112f493208a69edd002fcc3b5194ae1643a18c55:0]]

rows.text:
People most often forgot when the photo was taken, then the exact place, and sometimes which app/account held it [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]].
Interpretation: The stories cannot say where in the journey forgetting happens, and coder agreement on outcome is too low to use; this only describes what details were missing from public stories.

11% (13 of 115) mention forgetting the date or year; 3% (4 of 115) the exact place or venue; 1% (1 of 115) which app/account in core; adjacent adds 26% (57 of 216) which app/account and 8% (18 of 216) album [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|adjacent.q:2.4=album@photo_class:_all]].

One story captures the time gap: "I can't find any photos of me when I was 21" [[story|bb22e350914583e0d83bdffc9f3f46240abcf996:0]].

This is a share of public stories, not a user rate [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]].

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do people formulate searches when their memory is incomplete (i.e., what kinds of queries and strategies do they use when they only vaguely remember a photo)?
rows.gap: the stories hold nothing on how this ranks as an opportunity; the two AI coders agreed too little on metric_node to report it as a finding; the two AI coders agreed too little on question 2.1 to report it as a finding
rows.text:
People fall back to short, fuzzy cues — often a single noun — and then mix in modes like scrolling when that stalls [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=timeline_scroll@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=combined_search_then_scroll@photo_class:_all]].

17% (19 of 115) of core stories name a single noun; 20% (23 of 115) report typing keywords, and 12% (14 of 115) report timeline scrolling [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:4.1=single_noun@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=search_bar_keywords@photo_class:_all]], [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:3.2=timeline_scroll@photo_class:_all]].

One utility poster tries object terms — “Car Engine” — then runs into “wonky/useless ‘results’ includes ALOT (100s +) irrelevant results.” [[story|779a4ab6c05a566699aa57a7a0e44a5d88cf3d42:0]]

Interpretation: We cannot rank this as an opportunity, and cue-type details (who/what/when) have low reliability [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

*Want to see how this differs for sentimental photos?*

rows.text:
The engine can’t answer that. It only holds public stories people chose to post, not usage logs or user counts, so it cannot yield a success rate or a user-based percentage.

It covers what appears in posted stories and how often themes show up within that set. Your question needs metrics from representative usage or experiment data on searches from vague memories.

rows.text:
People most often say search did not understand what they typed, then they stall or try different wording, with some giving up without finding the pet photo [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

27% (31 of 115) of coded public stories first go wrong at “Does search understand it?” [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]].

One person wrote that "TEXT/SUBJECT search is FAIL" and results include "ALOT (100s +) irrelevant results" [[story|779a4ab6c05a566699aa57a7a0e44a5d88cf3d42:0]].

Interpretation: The stories do not isolate pet photos specifically, do not report what was collected, do not rank the opportunity, and coder agreement on outcome and question 2.1 was too low to trust those cuts [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]].

*Want to see how this splits by sentimentality vs utility?*
